info.desc: Autobahn (German for "motorway") is an album by Kraftwerk, released in 1974. The album’s 22-minute title track was edited to about 3 minutes for single release and reached #25 on the US Billboard charts, charting even higher around Europe, including #11 in the UK. This commercial success came after the band had released three highly experimental and purely instrumental albums. Autobahn is not a completely electronic album, as violin, flute, and guitar are used along with synthesizers. The title track features both untreated and vocoded vocals; the remaining tracks are purely instrumental. Kraftwerk used a Minimoog, an ARP Odyssey, an .

podcast.body: Kraftwerk released the song "Autobahn" in 1974, at a time when synthesizers were experiencing a brief craze. However, for Kraftwerk, this was not a novelty; their electronic music was a serious endeavor that demanded extensive study, engineering, and the development of new machines. "Autobahn in 1974. But to them this was hardly a novelty thing."

podcast.body: The title track of this 1974 album consumed the entire first side of the vinyl record, running for 22 minutes and 43 seconds. It exemplified the maximum length a single song could achieve on one side of a vinyl album during that era. "In 1974, Kraftwerk released an album called Autobahn, and the title track took up all of side one, 22 minutes and 43 seconds."

podcast.body: This album marked Kraftwerk's first worldwide success and was a pivotal point where the band shed any remaining traces of rock culture. It was highly impactful, notably influencing David Bowie, who played the album in full before his "Station to Station" tour shows. The album was a success in both the United States and Europe, solidifying their conceptual trajectory. "Autobahn fue un éxito en Estados Unidos y Europa, y comprendieron que esa senda conceptual era la que tenían que seguir."

podcast.body: This album was entirely electronic, and a drastically edited version of its 23-minute title track became a worldwide pop hit. The song itself is a simple ode to the joy of driving through the German countryside in a Volkswagen, with the band members recording the actual car sounds used on the record in their "People's Car." "In 1974, they released a totally electronic album entitled Autobahn, and a drastically edited version of the 23-minute title track became a worldwide pop hit."

podcast.body: This album, released in 1974, marked Kraftwerk's shift to an all-electronic sound, which was unprecedented at the time. Side 1 features a 23-minute title track, an homage to a Sunday drive on Germany's superhighways, incorporating instruments like the Mini-Moog, EMS Synthi, ARP Odyssey, and Florian Schneider's self-built Robovox. "In 1974 they released an all-electronic album. Nothing had ever sounded like this."
